title: Study plan
description: Discover subjects, structure, exams, teaching approach and much more of the Master in Cognitive Psychology in Health Communication offered by USI.

blocks.html:
Overview

The Master’s programme is designed to train students in psychology, with modules in Psychology, Communication, and Management.

The programme is organised into four semesters. During the fall semesters (1st and 3rd), students will attend classes taught at Università della Svizzera italiana, Lugano (USI), whereas courses in spring semesters (2nd and 4th) will be taught at Università Vita Salute San Raffaele, Milan (UNISR).

The first semester covers mainly classes in Health Communication and Research Methods, followed by topics in advanced Cognitive Psychology and Neuroscience and an internship in psychology during the second semester.

The third semester covers topics in Management, advanced aspects of Research, and an internship in psychology while during the fourth semester, students will attend selected topics in health and social psychology and write their Master’s Thesis under the joint supervision of both Faculties of UNISR/USI.

Study plan

The study plan and course descriptions provide an overview of the programme’s structure and content, and may be subject to changes.
Enrolled students should refer to the GESTU platform, where they can access the course offering, updated progressively each semester.

items.title: Curriculum description
items.html:
The study programme promotes a cross-sectoral approach over four semesters. Modules at USI and UNISR are divided into thematic areas that include compulsory and elective courses.

Elective courses and extra credits provide flexibility to the programme, allowing students to deepen their knowledge in research, clinical and cognitive psychology, and social health science.

The programme includes 120 ECTS, with modules in Psychology, Communication, and Management, as detailed in the study plan. Students must also acquire at least 8 ETCS of electives courses and 20 ECTS as practical applications in psychology and health communication.

Before discussing the Master’s thesis, the students take the final exam to become licensed psychologists in Italy. The exam will be held by a commission of psychologists at UNISR; it is mandatory for all students and requires a command of the Italian language. The programme ends with a final Master’s thesis in the broad area of psychology and health communication.

The programme is organised into four semesters:

  • The first semester covers mainly classes in Health Communication and Research Methods;
  • The second semester covers topics in advanced Cognitive Psychology and Neuroscience and an internship in psychology;
  • The third semester covers topics in Management, advanced aspects of Research, and an internship in psychology;
  • During the fourth semester, students will attend selected topics in health and social psychology and write their Master’s Thesis under the joint supervision of the Faculties of UNISR/USI;
  • Before discussing their thesis, students take the final exam to become licensed psychologists in Italy.

Over the two years, students will be supported by an active tutoring service.
